facts.program: SMUD My Energy Optimizer Partner+ battery enrollment incentive
facts.claim: One-time enrollment incentive: $500/kWh up to $10,000 for projects submitted by Sept 22, 2026 and enrolled by Dec 31, 2026; $300/kWh up to $6,000 for projects submitted on/after Sept 23, 2026. Requires Solar and Storage Rate and enrollment within 90 days of PTO.
facts.eligibility: Eguana, Enphase, Franklin, SolarEdge, Sonnen, Tesla batteries
facts.notes: There is NO separate '$5,400 SMUD battery rebate'. SMUD has no solar cash rebate (site's $2,000 claim unverified).

facts.claim: Heat pump HVAC up to $2,500/ton (from Nov 1, 2025); HPWH up to $2,500; VS pool pump $500 ($750 Jun 1-Sep 30, 2026); ENERGY STAR windows $2.00/sq ft; cool roof $0.20-$0.60/sq ft; whole house fan $200. Apply after install, within 12 months.
facts.notes: LADWP DOES rebate windows. No general LADWP battery rebate; batteries only via SGIP RSSE (<=80% AMI).

facts.claim: LADWP administers SGIP Residential Solar and Storage Equity funds for households at or below 80% AMI; solar+storage or storage added to existing solar.

Residential Solar and Storage Equity (RSSE) published at $1,100/kWh storage + $3,100/kW solar for low-income customers; Equity Resiliency $1,000/kWh. Availability varies by administrator (much of it waitlisted); general-market residential is not a reliable option.
facts.notes: The site's '$2,700-$13,500' and '$1,000+ for everyone' figures were unsourced; replaced with tier-dependent wording.

facts.claim: PG&E, SCE, SDG&E customers applying for new solar after April 14, 2023 are on the Net Billing Tariff; exports credited at hourly avoided-cost values, far below retail. SMUD and LADWP are not CPUC-regulated and set their own rules (SMUD Solar and Storage Rate).
